cards.explanation: The answer is that it cannot be moved. The psalm says, "Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever." (Psalm 125:1) Picture shoving a mountain, friends. You'd pull a muscle before it budged an inch, and I'd be the guy cheering from the sidelines, waving my mustache like a flag.

The answer is False. The psalm says Mount Zion "…cannot be moved; it abides forever." (Psalm 125:1) Forever and a season are not even in the same bakery, friends. Nobody ever called a mountain a limited-time offer.

The answer is people. "As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people…" (Psalm 125:2) Think of the mountains standing all the way around the city, friends. That's the picture of how the LORD surrounds them. I'd say that's a pretty great place to be standing.

The answer is from now on and forever. The psalm says the LORD surrounds His people "…both now and forevermore." (Psalm 125:2) No expiration date stamped on the box, friends. Nothing to check, nothing to toss when the date runs out.

The answer is so the righteous won't turn to injustice. The verse says the scepter of the wicked will not rest on the land, "…so that the righteous will not put forth their hands to injustice." (Psalm 125:3) That "so that" is the reason, friends, plain as flour on my apron.

The answer is that He would do good to them. The psalm prays, "Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart." (Psalm 125:4) Short and simple, friends. That prayer doesn't need a long wind-up, and I admire that, because I once gave a speech about one cookie and ran out of oven time.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "But those who turn to crooked ways the LORD will banish with the evildoers." (Psalm 125:5) It's a serious line, friends, so I'll just say it plainly. It sits right next to the prayer for the upright in heart.
